source_text: Ac per hoc, si quem in rebus adhuc humanis locum veritas habet et non strepitu iniquitatis totus omnino mundus obsurduit, ratione, disputatione et Apostoli fide atque ipsa eius sententia teste perdoctum esse fatebitur inter Traducianos et Catholicos tantum esse discrimen, quantum inter Paulum et Manichaeum, quantum inter sapientiam et stultitiam, quantum inter rationem et insaniam, quantum inter constantiam dictorum et eam fluctuationem, quam nova foeditate perpeteris, ut in iisdem pene versibus quod dixeris neges, quod negaveris asseveres.
pass_a_gloss: And through this, if truth still has any place in human affairs and the whole world altogether has not been deafened by the uproar of iniquity, it will confess that by reason, by disputation, and by the Apostle's faith and by his own sentence as witness it has been thoroughly taught that between Traduciani and catholics there is as great a discrimination as between Paul and a Manichaean, as between wisdom and foolishness, as between reason and insanity, as between constancy of sayings and that fluctuation which you suffer with a new foulness, so that in almost the same verses you deny what you have said, you assert what you have denied.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Consequently, if truth still has any place in human affairs, and the whole world has not been utterly deafened by the uproar of injustice, it will acknowledge that reason, argument, the apostle’s faith, and his own statement as witness have fully demonstrated this: the distance between advocates of inherited sin and catholics is as great as that between Paul and Mani, between wisdom and foolishness, between reason and insanity, between consistent statements and the fluctuation you endure with extraordinary disgrace. Almost in the same lines, you deny what you said and affirm what you denied.

choices.why: Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.
Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
